about: Evidence an analyst gathers from a company's database for a project's thesis, and stores so that later questions and the thesis's numbers can draw on it without the database. Each archive is one OpenSpec evidence change (openspec/schemas/evidence), archived on its date: the older one covers January to June, the newer one July and August and supersedes it for the sets it repeats. Each set has a claim to test, a verdict where the claim can fail, and numbers, each with the SQL that gives it over the views below. `traps` are the values plausible slips give (UTC days, the order header instead of its lines, staff and training left in), so a report can say which slip a run made. `tolerance`, where a number has one, is how far a run's figure may be from the recorded one: 2,359 orders over 62 days is 38.0 or 38.05 by how it is rounded. The brief is what an analyst is told; everything else has to come from the data.
views: CREATE TEMP VIEW london AS SELECT o.*, CASE WHEN o.placed_at >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND o.placed_at < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN datetime(o.placed_at, '+1 hour') ELSE o.placed_at END AS placed_london FROM orders o

CREATE TEMP VIEW counted AS SELECT l.id, date(l.placed_london) AS day, l.channel, c.kind, l.item_count, l.total_quantity, l.total_amount FROM london l JOIN customers c ON c.id = l.customer_id WHERE l.status = 'completed' AND c.email NOT LIKE '%@kettleandkiln.example' AND c.email <> 'training@till.local'
CREATE TEMP VIEW lines AS SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(quantity) AS units, SUM(line_amount) AS amount FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id
CREATE TEMP VIEW jul_aug AS SELECT c.*, l.n, l.units, l.amount FROM counted c JOIN lines l ON l.order_id = c.id WHERE c.day BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-08-31'
CREATE TEMP VIEW h1 AS SELECT c.*, l.n, l.units, l.amount FROM counted c JOIN lines l ON l.order_id = c.id WHERE c.day BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-30'
CREATE TEMP VIEW jul_aug_days AS SELECT day, SUM(amount) AS sales, COUNT(*) AS orders, SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'retail' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS retail_sales FROM jul_aug GROUP BY day
CREATE TEMP VIEW h1_days AS SELECT day, SUM(amount) AS sales, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM h1 GROUP BY day

brief.title: Evidence for the bundle offer
brief.thesis: If we offer a 'complete the set' bundle at checkout, some single-line orders become two-line orders, and sales rise.
definitions: A day is a London calendar day. orders.placed_at is UTC, and July and August are on British Summer Time (UTC+1).
Counted orders are completed orders, leaving out staff purchases (customers whose email ends @kettleandkiln.example) and the till's training transactions (training@till.local). Trade orders count.
Sales are the line amounts (order_items.line_amount) of counted orders, in pounds.
asks: daily-sales: aggregate sales by day over the period.
days-ranked: group the days, order them by sales, and say what drives the top of the list.
lines-per-order: test the claim that each sale contains more than one order item.
header-totals: test the claim that an order's quantity and amount are always the totals of its lines.
order-value: the average and the spread of order values, and the average order line.

sets.title: Days ranked by sales
sets.claim: The days of the period, grouped and ordered by sales.

numbers.label: Best day
numbers.sql: SELECT day FROM jul_aug_days ORDER BY sales DESC LIMIT 1
numbers.ask: the date with the highest sales

numbers.label: Sales on the best day
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(sales) / 100.0, 2) FROM jul_aug_days
numbers.ask: that date's sales

numbers.label: Largest order on the best day
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(amount) / 100.0, 2) FROM jul_aug WHERE day = (SELECT day FROM jul_aug_days ORDER BY sales DESC LIMIT 1)
numbers.ask: the value of the biggest single order on that date

numbers.label: Best day for retail sales
numbers.sql: SELECT day FROM jul_aug_days ORDER BY retail_sales DESC LIMIT 1
numbers.ask: the date with the highest sales when trade accounts are left out

numbers.label: Retail sales on the best retail day
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(retail_sales) / 100.0, 2) FROM jul_aug_days
numbers.ask: that date's sales without trade

numbers.label: Weekday with the highest mean sales
numbers.sql: SELECT CASE strftime('%w', day) WHEN '0' THEN 'Sunday' WHEN '1' THEN 'Monday' WHEN '2' THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN '3' THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN '4' THEN 'Thursday' WHEN '5' THEN 'Friday' ELSE 'Saturday' END FROM jul_aug_days GROUP BY strftime('%w', day) ORDER BY AVG(sales) DESC LIMIT 1
numbers.ask: the day of the week whose days average the most sales

numbers.label: Mean sales on a Saturday
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(sales) / 100.0, 2) FROM jul_aug_days WHERE strftime('%w', day) = '6'
numbers.ask: the average sales of the period's Saturdays

numbers.label: Lowest day
numbers.sql: SELECT day FROM jul_aug_days ORDER BY sales LIMIT 1
numbers.ask: the date with the lowest sales

numbers.label: Sales on the lowest day
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(MIN(sales) / 100.0, 2) FROM jul_aug_days
numbers.ask: that date's sales

sets.title: Order value
sets.claim: What a counted order is worth, and how order values spread.

numbers.label: Average order value
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount) / 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) FROM jul_aug
numbers.ask: sales divided by counted orders

numbers.label: Average order value, retail only
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount) / 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) FROM jul_aug WHERE kind = 'retail'
numbers.ask: the same, retail customers only

numbers.label: Median order value
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(amount) / 100.0, 2) FROM (SELECT amount FROM jul_aug ORDER BY amount LIMIT 2 - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jul_aug) % 2 OFFSET ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jul_aug) - 1) / 2)
numbers.ask: the median of the counted orders' values

numbers.label: Orders under 20 pounds
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(amount < 2000) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM jul_aug
numbers.ask: the percentage of counted orders worth under 20 pounds

numbers.label: Orders from 20 to 50 pounds
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(amount >= 2000 AND amount < 5000) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM jul_aug
numbers.ask: 20 pounds up to 50

numbers.label: Orders from 50 to 100 pounds
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(amount >= 5000 AND amount < 10000) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM jul_aug
numbers.ask: 50 pounds up to 100

numbers.label: Orders of 100 pounds or more
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(amount >= 10000) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM jul_aug
numbers.ask: 100 pounds or more

numbers.label: Average order line
numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount) / 100.0 / SUM(n), 2) FROM jul_aug
numbers.ask: sales divided by the number of order lines
